How the landscape is built ↗
Each pair contributes one fusion-path dissimilarity. All 1,326 values define the affinity matrix used for clustering and spectral embedding. U = −log(mean affinity to the other 51 systems). Selecting a pair highlights two systems in this fixed global landscape.
Path deviation, roughness, endpoint gaps and chaos loss enter the distance with equal weight after percentile ranking. Failed evaluations remain gaps. The surface interpolates the measured system heights for display.

Credits & scientific notes
Motivation is a conceptual analogy inspired by Gatys et al. (2015), not a reproduction of their experimental output. Mona Lisa: Leonardo da Vinci, public domain via Wikimedia Commons. Style: Juan Gris, Fantômas (1915), National Gallery of Art, Washington, CC0. Fusion portrait: newly generated illustration using both references. Artwork sources.
The two fusion galleries use nine weights from the pair-specific classification benchmark (Sec. IV). The earlier five-weight Fig. 2/11 examples and additional content–style experiments remain in the downloadable data. Trajectories are re-integrated from saved full-precision equations. Signatures retain their archived experiment values; Kaplan–Yorke dimensions are derived from those spectra.
The similarity landscape uses a fixed spectral embedding; U describes average affinity and the surface is display interpolation, not a physical potential. Input-layer time-reversal symmetry does not establish general symmetry of learned features.
HP ecology refers to the projected model; perturbation signatures refer to projected Lorenz-family models. SEIRS β/γ does not automatically give the full R₀ after equation changes. Original research figures and paper: CC BY 4.0.
